heroStrategy.headline: Create High-Quality AI Images & Videos with ByteDance Generative Models
heroStrategy.subheadline: Unlock the power of next-generation generative AI with Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro — built for professional visual content creation with precision, speed, and control.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use a full-bleed orange hero with a premium operational-dashboard treatment rather than a split image layout. Place the copy in a left-aligned text block over the bright field, and build the right side as a layered creation cockpit: framed preview windows, one static image tile, two video preview cards with play indicators, and slim performance meters. Keep the interface airy with white and charcoal panels, rounded corners, and subtle grid lines. This should feel like an enterprise-grade visual production workspace, not a generic AI showcase. CTA buttons must be orange-based, with the primary CTA solid and the secondary CTA outlined in charcoal/white. Add soft motion on chips and cards for a high-end, controlled feel.

repetitionBreakers: Start with a full-bleed orange hero and immediately follow with a dark proof band to avoid same-surface repetition.
Use tabbed product exploration for Seedream 4.5, then switch to a split-panel video module for Seedance 1.5 Pro.
Insert a charcoal capability strip before pricing to create contrast and reset attention.
Use a carousel for testimonials instead of a static grid to change pacing.
Close with a centered floating lead form after a card-based pricing section for a final visual shift.
blueprint.pageTitle: Seedream 4.5 and Seedance 1.5 Pro | AI Image & Video Generation
blueprint.metaDescription: Create high-quality AI images and videos with ByteDance generative models. Explore Seedream 4.5 for image generation and Seedance 1.5 Pro for synchronized video creation, pricing, testimonials, and enterprise-ready demo access.

sections.backgroundTreatment: full-bleed orange field with subtle overlay dashboard shell, floating generation chips, and a faint preview frame to imply live creative output
sections.designNote: PrimaryGoal: immediate capability recognition and premium control. NarrativeMode: product-led, high-energy launch. TrustStrategy: credibility through model sophistication rather than badges. VisualDominance: hero-product but still message-first due to long headline. ctaAggression: strong. sectionDensity: moderate. recommendedHeroStyle: dynamic full-bleed command-center hero with compact copy stack and one bold CTA.

Create an early dark proof band with rotating capability claims instead of logos: AI image generation, AI video generation with audio, multimodal content creation, enterprise-ready infrastructure, and professional output quality. This compensates for missing social proof while giving the page a strong confidence reset.

Use a two-part product block with alternating internal layouts. Seedream 4.5 should open first as the flagship module using tabs with a preview panel for text-to-image, editing, composition, resolution, and typography. Seedance 1.5 Pro should switch to a split-panel list with a cinematic preview strip to change rhythm and emphasize audio-video synchronization, lip-sync, and speed. Keep the first product more interactive and the second more operational.

Because the provided content has no why-techjockey points, repurpose this section as an enterprise reassurance panel: procurement simplicity, demo support, evaluation clarity, and workflow fit. Use a compact card grid with metric-like labels to preserve utility without fabricating testimonials or logos.

Present pricing as a focused two-card comparison with the Seedance plan visually emphasized through the stated starting price. Keep the layout clean and enterprise-friendly, with one highlighted card and one standard card so the page feels decisive without becoming salesy.

Use a testimonial carousel because there are 5 quotes. Make this section visually distinct with a dark background and large quote treatment. Rotate between creative director, video producer, art director, and marketing lead perspectives to reinforce cross-team value and reduce repetition.

End with a centered floating lead card rather than a split form. This creates a calmer conversion moment after the dark testimonial band. Keep CTA repetition controlled but clear, using the main action and a short reassurance line about demo access or quote request.

typography.heroFontSizeReason: The hero headline is long, so a smaller size keeps the layout clean and premium without line breaks dominating the fold.

colours.colourReason: Brand rules require using the provided primary color as the hero background and primary CTA color. The brand palette is orange, white, charcoal, and light grey, so the visual identity is built entirely from those values. Orange is used as the main energy signal, while white and soft grey keep the enterprise interface clean and readable.

referenceMap.cardStyle: Form-card and content modules use clean rectangular containers with functional, low-decoration styling; emphasis is on readability and conversion rather than elevated visual treatments like glass, shadows, or image-heavy cards.

referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Feature-led product presentation with each product represented as a self-contained section: label, headline, descriptive paragraph, primary CTA when needed, then a list of capability bullets. The pattern supports progressive disclosure through stacked feature groups.

Structure suggests a conversion-focused card with a section headline, hidden tracking fields, and compact field grouping. Best reused as a separate high-contrast form block rather than inline within narrative content.

designNotes: Prioritize conversion clarity over visual complexity.
Use a compact hero with high information density and short bullet reinforcement.
Keep feature modules modular and reusable with consistent label/headline/description hierarchy.
Reserve strong hierarchy for the main headline and primary CTA; secondary content should remain scannable.
Maintain a clean enterprise landing-page feel with minimal ornamentation.

Pricing or quote blocks for both products
Customer testimonial strip to reinforce credibility

avoidPatterns: Overly decorative or artsy layouts that reduce clarity
Long editorial storytelling before showing product value
Trust signals only at the bottom of the page
Cluttered multi-column comparisons that slow scanning
Generic stock visuals that do not demonstrate AI output

designStrategy.reasoning: This page should function as a high-conversion lead-generation asset for a solution-aware audience already interested in generative AI. The content is product-heavy and technical, so the design should stay product-led and proof-oriented, with the hero focused on a sharp message rather than brand storytelling. Because there are two related products, the page should present them in a stacked, easy-to-scan structure with strong CTA repetition and a testimonial-first trust approach. The gallery requirement is important: include visible image and video examples early to prove output quality and reduce friction. A split hero works best because it supports concise messaging on one side and visual proof on the other, while maintaining a professional, enterprise-ready tone.

strengths: Design planned from strategy and intent layers
